_note: Lift and throughput for closure (when the last ton arrives); see lift.py and the Lift layer spec in the Program Hub. Every figure is marked: 'illustrative' means chosen by Claude for the demo, not a planning factor. Change a figure here and nothing else: no code change is needed. Stage 1: the starting set sits at the origin, ready on D+0.

ships._note: Capacity in short tons only; deck area is not modelled (decided 25 Nov 2026). Sailing time is the route's, at the carrier speed in movement_rules.json; the ship type sets only how much one load carries.

sources.capacity_st: illustrative. For reference only: 312,461 sq ft of deck (T-AKR 295), https://man.fas.org/dod-101/sys/ship/takr-295.htm, opened 25 Nov 2026; deck area is not used

aircraft._note: Planning payload (allowable cabin load), not the maximum in air_rules.json: planners use it on long legs. Ground hours are per stop, block-in to block-out.

sources.planning_payload_st: illustrative: a Gemini summary of AFPAM 10-1403 gave 75 to 85 short tons, unverified (no table or page)
sources.ground_hours: illustrative: the same summary gave 4 to 6 hours, unverified

sources.planning_payload_st: illustrative: the same summary gave '145.0 short tons (~90,000 lbs)'; 90,000 lb is 45 short tons. Unverified
sources.ground_hours: illustrative: the same summary gave 2.25 to 3.25 hours, unverified

ports._note: Short tons a day a port can load or discharge, by World Port Index harbor size (the WPI has no rates). '' is a port with no size.

airfields._note: Working MOG: aircraft an airfield can load or unload at once, by OurAirports type. Sorties a day = working MOG x 24 / ground hours.
